method: Static reverse engineering only; specimens were never executed.

external_evidence.availability: Reports inaccessible through web tool. Sandbox scores and family signatures were treated as leads, not verdict evidence.

samples.identification: CyberGate RAT with embedded UPX-packed payload

managed_reverse_engineering.comparison: Decompiled files differ only in C2_URL; no family attribution is inferred from self-assigned BlackCat/HiddenTears/malware mutex strings.
managed_reverse_engineering.entry_path: Main creates hidden ProgramData working directories, locks the workstation, shows the payment window, blocks input and schedules a startup HTTP report. It invokes disabling, persistence, surveillance and impact helpers without an opt-in UI.
verified_paths: StartKeylogger installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL. HookCallback appends key names to KEYLOG_FILE. A separate thread polls keys 1..255 using GetAsyncKeyState and appends observed keys every 50 ms.

ContinuousDataExfiltration reads KEYLOG_FILE/CLIP_FILE, truncates the payloads, and passes objects to SendToC2. SendToC2 serializes JSON and submits FormUrlEncodedContent through HttpClient.PostAsync to C2_URL.

ConstantDataScraping recursively enumerates drives and reads files up to 1 MiB; Base64 data is truncated to 2000 characters and sent with the original path through SendToC2. StealCookies reads the Chrome Cookies database and transmits a truncated Base64 representation.

ContinuousScreenshot saves periodic desktop JPEGs. ReadBrowserData copies Cookies, History and Login Data to .stolen files. AccessWindowsCredentialManager copies Microsoft Credentials directory files; it does not decrypt them.

InstallPersistence writes the current image to a Run key, copies it to Startup and launches schtasks with /sc onlogon. USBWorm copies the image to ready removable drives and writes executable AutoRun configuration.

DisableDefenderPowerShell Base64-encodes UTF-16LE Set-MpPreference commands and launches hidden PowerShell. DeleteShadowCopies launches VSSADMIN and WMIC deletion commands. Service/hosts/policy helpers attempt further disruption.

BypassUAC writes ms-settings shell open-command and DelegateExecute values, launches fodhelper and schedules key cleanup. This proves a hijack attempt, not successful elevation; the global mutex can stop a second image.

RealEncryption selects Desktop/TestFolder files, calls EncryptAES, then would write a suffixed replacement and delete the original. AES_KEY is 17 bytes and AES_IV is 15 bytes: the key assignment fails before replacement or deletion. This is an attempted ransomware path, not successful encryption.

ProcessInjection writes only a RET byte into notepad and starts a remote thread. This helper is a demonstration stub, not proof of injected theft. The unrelated NetworkSpread helper is uncalled and uses loopback administrative shares.
limitations: ClipboardMonitor requests CF_TEXT but interprets the pointer as Unicode.
Filesystem, registry, service and shadow-copy operations can fail on access checks; attempted effects are distinguished from successful ones.
RansomwareSimulation event-log strings and test-directory scoping do not negate the reachable input capture, uploads and lockout.

resource_decode.note: Field indices are interpreted from the executable code, not used as detection thresholds.

verified_paths: Outer entry0 at 0x40bbf4 checks update/password-list/block-input mutex modes, loads and decodes configuration, selects autostart/injection behavior, writes the payload sidecar configuration and enters the payload handoff.

Manual PE mapper at 0x4040f4 reads PE headers, allocates/maps the image and invokes remote-thread preparation; 0x4038ac invokes CreateRemoteThread. Configuration injection mode is 1; explorer.exe is also a configured alternative target, not evidence it is selected in this mode.

Password-list mutex mode calls 0x409ef8, loads NSS, resolves NSSBase64_DecodeBuffer/PK11_GetInternalKeySlot/PK11_Authenticate/PK11SDR_Decrypt, locates profiles.ini and legacy signons files, decrypts stored credential records and stages FIREFOX.abc. Other branches collect Windows/IE/MSN/No-IP secrets.

The outer keyboard callback at 0x40b0b8 calls GetKeyboardState and ToAscii but discards the character and returns 1. The companion mouse callback also returns 1. This is input blocking; hook plus ToAscii does not establish keylogging.

The extracted field-100 PE has UPX0/UPX1 layout and decompresses successfully with UPX. Its socket receive wrapper at 0x14012bf4 calls recv at 0x14012c32. A receive loop at 0x14029064 assembles delimited data.

The unpacked operator dispatcher at 0x14034a34 handles shellativar, shellresposta, keyloggergetlog and getpassword. The getpassword branch at 0x1403b3ff creates the password-list mutex at 0x1403b4d6 and relaunches the outer executable at 0x1403b515, reaching the credential-harvesting mode. Socket send/receive/connect and shell/keylog/webcam control paths corroborate the CyberGate identity.

Anti-analysis helpers for guest artifacts and debugger devices exist, but the recovered individual anti-analysis flags at indices 45..56 are FALSE. API and service-name presence does not establish that those checks execute.
native_reverse_engineering.resource_metric_correction: Rizin enumerates 19 RT_ICON leaf images, two icon groups and three RCDATA entries. Cleave pe.icon_count=2 and pe.resource_count=3 are parser metrics, not counts of all resource leaves. Revised descriptions explicitly say parser icon count.
native_reverse_engineering.verdict_basis: Operator-triggered credential harvesting and the mapped remote-control payload, independent of filenames, ML probabilities, sandbox scores or third-party signatures.

corrected_inferences: Hook/ToAscii co-occurrence moved from hostile keylogging to notable window-hook API profile.
Unsigned VBoxService/mutex/injection API co-occurrence moved from hostile evasion to notable remote-thread API profile.
Resource/temp/ShellExecute/Run-key co-occurrence moved from hostile persistence to notable registry API profile.
Packed NSS fragment matcher now requires a broken NSS_Init name instead of matching an intact plaintext NSS_Init.
Low icon count is described as the parser metric; no assertion of few icon leaf images.
placement: Remote-thread primitives and their umbrella moved from inject/dll and inject/runtime/call to inject/remote-thread; exact consumers updated.
Encoded VirtualAlloc and VirtualProtect references moved from dylib/lookup to their memory operation homes.
XOR VirtualAlloc reference moved from anti-static/decoders to mem/alloc/virtual and made notable; no required concealment beyond encoding.
trait_changes.scope_audit: Moved atomic and composite matchers preserve their effective scopes and exclusions. Remote-thread mapping uses parent T1055 rather than DLL-injection T1055.001. The Python allocation/write/thread chain no longer claims a DLL payload. The broad objectives/evasion/process/injection selector in PowerShell Empire loses the old native PE-only generic profile intentionally; no new neutral alternative is added as evasion evidence. Other affected consumers use exact IDs and are updated explicitly.
trait_changes.no_dependency_fetch: These are native/managed PE samples, with no fetched-dependency PURL behind the reviewed findings.

verification.limitations: Controls prove matching requirements and near misses, not whole-program semantics. An independent original packed NSS specimen is not available in this queue; the new packed-name boundary has a synthetic positive and plaintext negative control.
